current.text: He enters his third season. Nikola Vucevic, Coby White and coach Billy Donovan are gone, and Tiago Splitter is the new head coach.

He is in the projected starting five with Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton. With Claxton at center and Wilson at the four, he moves down to small forward on a big-focused roster.
When he got more minutes late last season, he ranked about 50th in 9-cat, with 19 points, 7 rebounds, 3 threes and almost 2 blocks in 31 minutes.
Experts expect his minutes to rise to about 32 a game and see no playing-time worry. They expect his usage to land below his late-season peak but above his early-season level.
Splitter is expected to give him more ball handling and point forward duties, so his assists should go up. How much Splitter will empower him is still an open question.
In preseason he has shown almost no rebounds and very low usage, while the Bulls feed usage to Caleb Wilson.
Experts disagree on his share of the ball. One sees him second on the team in usage, ahead of Giddey and Wilson. Another expects Norman Powell to lead the team in usage, with Buzelis lower.
Several experts think his blocks may drop next to Caleb Wilson and at small forward, even with more minutes.
He hurt his ankle in preseason. It does not appear serious, and he has no Yahoo injury status.
Experts rank him as a top-50 player in 9-cat, in a range of about 40 to 60. They expect him to finish around 50 and call him more polished than Caleb Wilson.
The experts say the market still underrates him, even after his Yahoo rank rose into the 60s. He is the best fantasy target on the Bulls and should be the first player taken from his draft class.
Draft advice: do not take him around pick 40. Around pick 60 is good value and around 80 would be a steal. His auction price should be about 20 USD.
In an expert auction mock he went for 22 USD. The expert is a big fan but would only pay value.
Chicago is expected to be a bad team, probably bottom ten in the league. One prediction is 32 wins.
The Bulls played very fast late last season and are expected to play an up-tempo transition style.
Chicago has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. With a March 28 end, they play 3, 3 and 4 games (10) in our playoff weeks.

durable.text: Blocks are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool and even further above other forwards.
He makes many threes for a forward, but his three-point percentage is modest (about 35%). His threes come from volume, not accuracy.

note: Experts agree he is a top-50 9-cat player and say his auction price should be about 20 USD. That is well above the market's average cost of about 6 USD and the 12 USD he went for in our league last season, and an expert mock sold him for 22 USD. He has no weak category flags, and his blocks plus threes from the forward spot make him an easy fit for most builds. Paying up to about 20 USD is fine, but do not go far past it. Early in the season, check that his minutes reach about 32 and his usage holds next to Powell and Wilson, since he showed few rebounds and low usage in preseason. Also watch whether his blocks hold at small forward.
